root_idea.summary: The root centers on stillness: movement or activity comes to rest, and something remains settled or fixed in place.
root_idea.development: This core extends from still water, wind, ships, and people to equilibrium, subsiding heat or effervescence, and nouns for fixed objects and resting places. Figurative extensions associate settled fullness or a constant supply with the same notion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is normalized to the supported singular active-participle citation form.

senses.usage_conditions: The attested Quranic plural describes ships left motionless on the sea when the wind is stilled; the participial sense is of something remaining fixed rather than moving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become still, motionless, fixed, or stationary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water, wind, ships—including a ship becoming aground—and people; of people, it can also include becoming silent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To subside or cease active motion: expressed grape juice stops effervescing, and heat abates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are specialized applications of the verb to grape juice and heat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become balanced, reaching equilibrium.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a balance or scales.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a pulley sheave, to become fixed; in another usage, to turn or revolve.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two applications are reported as contrary uses of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, to reach its midday height or remain overhead as though it did not leave its place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional description of the sun at or around midday.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, for good fortune to cease and circumstances to begin gradually declining.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for a people's wind becoming still, with the wind representing their good fortune and affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render something still or motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited causative use is applied to water and similar things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become still or motionless by degrees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the gradual-development use of the Form VI verb.
Said of a bowl or large serving vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Constant and unceasing in milk supply.
The three stones on which a cooking pot is set.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This plural noun is associated with the stones remaining fixed in their places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Places where a person or thing remains still; also depressed or hollow parts of the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The first sense is the plural of مَرْكَد; the second applies to low-lying depressions in the ground.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form I unit contains the core stillness meaning and several distinct conventional applications.
The still, fixed, non-running sense of رَاكِد and its plural is covered by the Quran-attested sense.
Specialized plural noun for the pot-supporting stones.
Places of stillness and depressed parts of the earth.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is a plural form, while the public headword is normalized to the supported singular active-participle citation form.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: maqayis:row:2123 reports, conditionally ('if sound'), an anomalous usage of تَرَاكَدَ involving seated maidens; its authenticity and relation to the normal root development are explicitly uncertain, so it is not assigned a public sense.
